messages.content:
The numbers 1, 2, ..., 2100 are written on a board. Every second, Mark takes two numbers on the board, \( a \) and \( b \), erases them, and replaces them with \( \gcd(a, b) \) and \( \operatorname{lcm}(a, b) \). Mark stops once any move he makes will not change the numbers written on the board. Compute the number of divisors of the 2026th smallest positive integer written on the board when he finishes.

Put your final answer within \boxed{}.

message.content:
Looking at this problem, I need to understand what happens when Mark repeatedly replaces pairs $(a,b)$ with $(\gcd(a,b), \text{lcm}(a,b))$.

## Key Invariants

**Product preservation:** Since $a \cdot b = \gcd(a,b) \cdot \text{lcm}(a,b)$, the product of all numbers stays $2100!$.

**Per-prime exponent multisets:** For each prime $p$, the multiset of $p$-exponents is invariant, since replacing $(e_1, e_2)$ with $(\min(e_1,e_2), \max(e_1,e_2))$ preserves the multiset.

## Characterizing the Final State

Mark stops when no move changes anything, meaning every pair satisfies $a \mid b$ or $b \mid a$. The final configuration is a **divisibility chain** $n_1 \mid n_2 \mid \cdots \mid n_{2100}$.

For a divisibility chain, $p$-exponents must be **non-decreasing** across all positions. Since the multiset of $p$-exponents is fixed, the final state is **uniquely determined**:

$$n_i = \prod_p p^{e_i^{(p)}}$$

where $e_i^{(p)}$ is the $i$-th smallest $p$-exponent among $\{v_p(1), v_p(2), \ldots, v_p(2100)\}$.

## Computing $e_{2026}^{(p)}$ for Each Prime

I need the 2026th value in the sorted list. The number of values $\leq k$ is $2100 - \lfloor 2100/p^{k+1}\rfloor$. I need the smallest $k$ where this $\geq 2026$, i.e., $\lfloor 2100/p^{k+1}\rfloor \leq 74$.

| Prime $p$ | $\lfloor 2100/p \rfloor$ | Zeros | $\lfloor 2100/p^2 \rfloor$ | Cumulative through 1 | $e_{2026}^{(p)}$ |
|-----------|--------------------------|-------|----------------------------|----------------------|-----------------|
| 2 | 1050 | 1050 | 525 | 1575 | **4** (pos 1970–2035) |
| 3 | 700 | 1400 | 233 | 1867 | **3** (pos 2024–2075) |
| 5 | 420 | 1680 | 84 | 2016 | **2** (pos 2017–2084) |
| 7 | 300 | 1800 | 42 | 2058 | **1** |
| 11 | 190 | 1910 | 17 | 2083 | **1** |
| 13 | 161 | 1939 | 12 | 2088 | **1** |
| 17 | 123 | 1977 | 7 | 2093 | **1** |
| 19 | 110 | 1990 | 5 | 2095 | **1** |
| 23 | 91 | 2009 | 3 | 2097 | **1** |
| 29 | 72 | 2028 | — | — | **0** (2026 ≤ 2028) |
| $p \geq 31$ | $\leq 67$ | $\geq 2033$ | — | — | **0** |

## Computing $n_{2026}$

$$n_{2026} = 2^4 \cdot 3^3 \cdot 5^2 \cdot 7^1 \cdot 11^1 \cdot 13^1 \cdot 17^1 \cdot 19^1 \cdot 23^1$$

## Counting Divisors

$$\tau(n_{2026}) = (4+1)(3+1)(2+1)(1+1)^6 = 5 \cdot 4 \cdot 3 \cdot 64 = 3840$$

$$\boxed{3840}$$
